title: When the Typewriter Burns
premise: In the river city of Vellmara, on the eve of revolution, Sebastian Ishikawa lives as a boy in her father's print shop, cutting typefaces by day and hiding pamphlets by night. When soldiers close the bridge for the winter season and seize the shop's ledgers as evidence against the printers' guild, Sebastian discovers his father's name at the top of the arrest list. To save him, Sebastian must carry a single printed page — proof that the governor forged the sedition charges — through three checkpoints before the first snow seals the passes. He succeeds at terrible cost: the typewriter burns, his father escapes, but Sebastian chooses to stay behind in Vellmara, finally claiming both his name and his place among the people he once hid from.
about_author: Sebastian Amberdale is the pen name of a former letterpress apprentice who spent a decade restoring antique printing equipment in Central European mill towns. Their novels explore what ordinary hands do when history arrives uninvited.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Sebastian Ishikawa introduces the print shop's rhythms: sorting type, binding pamphlets, passing as the cutter's son in a city that asks no questions it can't answer. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: the fragile comfort of invisibility, already cracking under the sound of distant drums.

chapters.title: Orders Come at Dusk
chapters.summary: A government courier delivers the closure notice for the bridge and a warrant listing guild printers, Sebastian's father among them. The family burns what they can, but the ledgers are seized. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: dread arriving with bureaucratic politeness; the moment safety becomes a memory.

chapters.title: What the Governor Signed
chapters.summary: Sorting salvaged type, Sebastian finds a misprinted proof sheet bearing the governor's true signature date — proof the sedition charges were backdated. His father insists it must reach the magistrate across the river. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: reluctant awakening; knowledge as burden.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints, One Page
chapters.summary: Sebastian maps the route: the fish market gate, the customs house, the bridge itself. An old smuggler named Maren agrees to teach him the blind spots — for a price he cannot yet pay. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into purpose; first taste of belonging to something larger.

chapters.title: The Fish Market Gate
chapters.summary: First crossing attempt. Sebastian hides the page inside a hollowed sort-case of broken type, but a soldier recognizes his father's face in him and lingers too long. He talks his way through using the shop's official credentials. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration braided together.

chapters.title: Maren's Price
chapters.summary: Maren reveals her price: the location of the guild's hidden press, which she intends to sell to whichever side wins. Sebastian must decide whether belonging requires betrayal. POV: alternating Sebastian and Maren. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; trust as currency spent in wartime.

chapters.title: Snow on the Customs House
chapters.summary: Second checkpoint. A blizzard delays the convoy, and Sebastian shelters overnight beside the very officer hunting his father, listening to the man describe the printer he means to break. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: hatred complicated by recognition; the enemy made human.

chapters.title: When the Typewriter Burns
chapters.summary: Soldiers torch the print shop to destroy remaining evidence. Sebastian watches from the crowd as his childhood burns, understanding that invisibility is over — everyone now knows whose child he is. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: grief as crucible; identity forged in fire.

chapters.title: The Bridge
chapters.summary: Climax. At the final checkpoint, Sebastian is searched; the page is nearly found until Maren, having chosen loyalty over profit, creates a diversion and is arrested in his place. Sebastian crosses as the season's last traveler before the ice closes. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: sacrifice witnessed; courage costing exactly what it should.

chapters.title: The Name I Keep
chapters.summary: The magistrate acts; the arrests are reversed and the governor flees. Sebastian returns to the burned shop, chooses to rebuild rather than leave, and signs the new guild ledger with his full name — both of them. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: resolution as self-claiming; belonging earned, not granted.
